notes: Built from USAspending spending_by_award search responses (POST, archived with request body in raw/manifest.jsonl, source_id usaspending-post). Amount = USAspending 'Award Amount' (cumulative federal obligation, not a ceiling and not an announced figure); disbursed_usd = 'Total Outlays' when present. Dates = 'Base Obligation Date' (first obligation), else 'Start Date'. Search was recipient-name text on awarding agency = Department of Energy over 2007-10-01..2026-09-30 and one page of up to 50 rows per award-type group; awards with zero or negative net obligation are omitted. Recipient name variants not matched by the name search may be missing. Government record, basis=disclosed. The DELP0000207 row is an LPO conditional commitment (USAspending description), not a closed loan; its 'Loan Value' is the committed face amount and must not be counted as funding received. DOE's announcement was not retrieved. VERIFIER (2026-10-05): every row re-checked against the archived search snapshot (amount, outlays, base obligation date all match) and against a per-award USAspending award-detail snapshot (api/v2/awards/<id>/, source verify-usaspending). Rows are award-level aggregates, so each event is one award, not a modification. Participant evidence now quotes the award's assistance-listing title or awarding office from the award-detail snapshot (the old quote only said 'Department of Energy'); obligated_usd now has its own evidence ("total_obligation"). Where the search row showed 'Total Outlays' 0.0 but the award detail has total_outlay null (no File C outlay reporting, typical for pre-2020 or brand-new awards), disbursed_usd was removed: 0.0 meant 'not reported', not 'nothing paid'. DELP0000207: award detail shows total_obligation 0.0, total_loan_value 262,881,867.11 and subsidy cost 1,359,099.25, consistent with a conditional commitment that has not been disbursed. It is therefore a ceiling. SHINE appears in both census files: fission (isotopes/back_end) and fusion (accelerator-driven D-T neutron source). The NNSA DENA awards are Mo-99 medical-isotope cooperative agreements with large non-federal cost share.
